findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve which child guarantees an unchanged DC body performs no pandoc spawn on a no-op pass — clarify whether rich_sha short-circuits the compare-time to_wire render in 3388, or assign the no-op-no-spawn property explicitly.
evidence: 5c0e: 'The change-gated "no-op → no pandoc spawn" property is delivered by the cutover/echo story 3388, which introduces the change-gated rich_sha render gate; that symbol ... is not this story's to add.'

3388: 'store a change-gated rich_sha ... so a re-render is only pushed when the wire actually changed. The compare stays comparison-only and never writes back.' — this gates the push, and 3388's compares route the LOCAL side through normalize_outbound = decode(to_wire(t)), which invokes the DC renderer (pandoc) during the compare regardless of rich_sha.
5c0e Context cites the ~0.3s/field spawn tax and a serial pass blocking ~20 min as the hazard being hardened, making per-pass no-op spawns material.
findings.finding: The 'no pandoc spawn on an unchanged (no-op) body' performance property appears owned by no child. 5c0e explicitly disclaims it (delivered by 3388's rich_sha), but 3388's rich_sha is described as a compare-only push gate ('The compare stays comparison-only') that gates the outbound PUSH, not the pandoc render invocation; the DC compare/fit itself invokes WikiTextCodec.to_wire (→ pandoc) each pass. Neither child asserts that an unchanged body avoids the pandoc subprocess spawn.
findings.location: child 5c0e-e25f-b14e-4aba (Prior art / dependency boundaries) and child 3388-96e8-e14e-4221 (rich_sha)
findings.suggested_fix: In 3388, state that a rich_sha match short-circuits the DC compare-side to_wire render (so no-op passes skip pandoc), or add an explicit child criterion (in 5c0e or 3388) asserting zero pandoc spawns on an unchanged body.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an AC (and test) that after the cutover flag is flipped OFF on a binding whose baseline has already advanced to the rich form, the next reconcile pass emits zero spurious description re-emit and no downgrade churn — asserting the post-rollback baseline interpretation, not merely that the wire reverted.
evidence: POST-ROLLBACK STATE clause: raise when the plan 'changes how existing persisted records are interpreted' — the cutover re-interprets the baseline as rich-decoded form.
shrew story: '_advance_baselines continues to advance the per-binding baseline from ctx.curr_snapshot at persist' — under the flag-ON codec path the baseline lands in rich form.
Rollback AC asserts the wire reverts (test_cutover_rollback_restores_plain) but is silent on the persisted baseline's interpretation on the next flag-OFF pass.
ABSENCE: no AC asserts a flag-OFF pass over a binding whose baseline already advanced to rich form emits zero spurious re-emit / no downgrade churn.
findings.finding: The description cutover advances the persisted per-binding baseline to the rich decoded form once the flag is ON, but the rollback ACs assert only that the outbound WIRE reverts to plain/identity when the flag is flipped OFF — neither the top-level plan nor the shrew story asserts on the baseline's state AFTER rollback. A baseline already advanced to rich form, then compared against a plain/identity-encoded local body (flag OFF), can re-report 'local changed' and cause a spurious re-emit / downgrade churn, particularly under the lossy DC codec whose baseline compare-space reasoning is scoped to the flag-ON codec path.
findings.location: Top-level plan 'Live cutover plus echo suppression' + disparaged-parodistic-shrew AC 'cutover is flag-gated ... reverts to the plain/identity wire when off; verified by test_cutover_defaults_off and test_cutover_rollback_restores_plain'
scenarios: Cloud or DC client cut over (flag ON), baselines advance to rich decoded form, then a bad-rollout rollback flips the flag OFF; the next reconcile pass compares plain-encoded local against a rich-form baseline.

DC lossy codec: the plan's baseline-compare-space cancellation argument assumes the flag-ON codec normalize_outbound is applied to the local side; with the flag OFF that normalization is gone but the stored baseline is still rich.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend disparaged-parodistic-shrew's rollback AC to assert the flag-OFF compare over an already-rich baseline converges (zero outbound), e.g. by having the flag-OFF path normalize both operands into the same space or by defining how a rich-form baseline is interpreted when the plain/identity path is restored; add a test test_rollback_over_advanced_baseline_no_churn covering both Cloud and the lossy DC codec.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm whether AC9's 'every corpus case' scope is intended to be a corpus-wide concurrency sweep; if so, add a child criterion running the concurrent-edit conflict assertion across the DC/Cloud corpora rather than a single representative body, or narrow the parent AC to 'a representative concurrent both-sides edit'.
evidence: Parent AC: 'Every corpus case with concurrent local plus remote edits emits a conflict instead of silently overwriting either side.'
3388 AC: 'A concurrent both-sides body edit keeps rebar's body (settled local-wins) AND raises the existing outbound-field-conflict bridge alert ... verified by test_concurrent_conflict_alerts.'
3388 Testing lists a single 'Concurrent: both sides edit the same body' scenario, not an enumeration over the corpus.
271c/e59d corpora tests cover idempotence/richness/byte-preservation, not concurrency; no sibling asserts a per-corpus-case conflict sweep.
findings.finding: Parent AC9 requires that EVERY corpus case with concurrent local+remote edits emits a conflict rather than silently overwriting, but child 3388's covering criterion asserts only a single hand-constructed both-sides concurrent edit (test_concurrent_conflict_alerts), not a corpus-wide sweep of every case. No sibling asserts the 'every corpus case' scope for concurrency.
findings.location: child 3388-96e8-e14e-4221 (Acceptance Criteria: concurrent both-sides body edit)
scenarios: A corpus body whose specific content triggers a codec normalization artifact makes local!=baseline AND remote!=baseline compare EQUAL after normalization, so the both-sides divergence is missed and one side is silently overwritten — undetected because only one representative case is tested.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add a corpus-driven concurrency test to 3388 (assert conflict/local-wins for each corpus case placed under a synthesized both-sides edit) or reword parent AC9 to match the single-case scope 3388 actually delivers.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the 'one-way Markdown→wiki renderer' phrasing with the 'bidirectional' title by explicitly stating what the DC inbound/pull path does (identity passthrough? no inbound rich-text decode?).
evidence: Title: 'Bidirectional Markdown ⇄ Jira rich-text sync (Cloud ADF + DC wiki)'
Design: 'DC is a one-way Markdown→wiki renderer with bidirectional synchronization.'
'Jira wiki markup is lossy for punctuation-dense prose, so the DC path must not rely on codec fixed points.'
findings.finding: The title promises 'Bidirectional Markdown ⇄ Jira rich-text sync' for both Cloud and DC, but the Design states 'DC is a one-way Markdown→wiki renderer with bidirectional synchronization', mixing 'one-way' and 'bidirectional' in one sentence. This tension is unresolved: DC cannot round-trip (wiki is lossy), yet the header and per-binding echo/conflict machinery imply bidirectional behavior. A reader cannot tell what DC's read/pull direction actually does.
findings.location: Design section; 'DC is a one-way Markdown→wiki renderer with bidirectional synchronization'
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify that DC rendering is one-way outbound while the bidirectional part is limited to echo-safety/conflict detection over baselines; state explicitly how inbound DC wiki content is handled.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the comment echo loop-breaker (RECONCILER_MARKER, an HTML comment) survives the Markdown-aware codec that drops HTML comments — either carry the description path's self-verify/plain-fallback into the comment codec path, move the marker out of codec-visible body content, or key echo suppression on the ID map/baseline state instead of the in-body marker; and state which in emersed-specific-mutt.
evidence: Parent: 'Use the same rich-text codec as descriptions' for comments (emersed-specific-mutt).

outbound_comments.py:78 RECONCILER_MARKER = '<!-- rebar:reconciler-echo -->'; :184 appends it into the comment body; :181 asserts 'The marker survives ADF round-trip (each paragraph maps to its own ADF node and back)' — true only for the plain adf.py encoder.
inbound_differ.py:337 `if RECONCILER_MARKER in body_text` is the load-bearing inbound echo filter; apply_inbound_records.py:329 mirrors it.

The child cutover ticket disparaged-parodistic-shrew documents that marklas drops HTML comments ('text <!-- x --> more' -> 'text  more'; a lone marker -> empty string) and that 'rebar's own <!-- rebar:reconciler-echo --> is an HTML comment, so any echo-suppression logic keying on that marker must not assume it survives a Markdown-aware encode.'
The parent applies a self-verify/plain-fallback mitigation to descriptions but never carries it to the comment marker path.
findings.finding: The comment echo loop-breaker relies on the HTML-comment marker RECONCILER_MARKER surviving a codec round-trip, but the Markdown-aware codec the parent routes comments through drops HTML comments, silently disabling the inbound echo filter.
findings.location: Child responsibilities → Append-only comments ('Use the same rich-text codec as descriptions'); Design → 'Origin-gated outbound'
scenarios: A rebar-originated comment is encoded through the Markdown-aware codec, the marker is stripped, the comment is read back inbound with no marker, and the inbound differ treats rebar's own echo as a new Jira comment — a comment loop or spurious mirror.
Echo suppression silently degrades to body-equality-only for comments, which the append-only ID map only partly covers for pre-map bodies.
findings.suggested_fix: In the comment story, key inbound echo suppression on the append-only local-key→Jira-ID map (already introduced) rather than on the in-body HTML-comment marker, OR mandate the same self-verifying plain-encode fallback the description path uses for any comment body whose marker does not survive re-decode.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify the pandoc/pypandoc-binary choice for the DC renderer against established pure-Python Markdown->Jira-wiki converters (e.g., md-to-jira, md-jira, pandoc's jira writer), explaining why an in-process, dependency-light option was rejected given the plan's own stdlib-only engine contract and the subprocess/GPL/SBOM hardening it forces.
evidence: Plan: 'Render safe units through pinned pypandoc-binary' and DC robustness introduces subprocess timeout, process-group kill, and GPL/SBOM obligations for the bundled binary.

Prior art retrieved: PyPI 'md-to-jira' ('fully self-contained, requiring no external libraries or dependencies'); GitHub 'larsq-public/md-jira' (bidirectional Markdown<->Jira wiki + ADF); pandoc's own jira writer / 'tupton/pandoc-jira-custom-writer'.

Plan's own contract rationale (DEVIATION): the engine importing adf.py is 'contractually dependency-free' (confirmed pyproject.toml lines 68-69: 'engine assets ... are stdlib-only'), which cuts AGAINST introducing a GPL subprocess binary for DC when in-process alternatives exist.
The plan justifies the Cloud dependency choice at length but gives NO comparable prior-art consideration for the DC renderer's pandoc dependency.
findings.finding: The DC Markdown->Jira-wiki renderer commits to a heavyweight bundled GPL pandoc subprocess (pypandoc-binary) without surveying established pure-Python, dependency-free Markdown->Jira-wiki converters, even though the plan's own central rationale is a stdlib-only engine contract that would favor an in-process solution.
findings.location: Design / 'DC renderer capability' + 'DC robustness' children; ashy-waterlog-hamadryas
scenarios: Reviewer/operator asks why a GPL subprocess binary and its full hardening surface (timeout, process-group kill, SBOM) is warranted when pure-Python converters exist.
Deployment environments where bundling/executing a GPL binary or spawning subprocesses is restricted.
